title: Spoke manifest
description:
An optional `.tcat-spoke.json` at the root of a data spoke, declaring which schema version it is written against and where its documents live.

It exists so that spoke LAYOUT is declarative rather than conventional. The validator's directory-name convention (`manifests/`, `calibrations/`, ...) is a default, not a requirement -- and a default that a real lab will have good reasons to diverge from. A spoke organised by campaign, by student, by instrument, or as a monorepo of several sub-projects is equally valid: the contract is per-RECORD, not per-repository.

That is the whole point. Whether the collaboration ends up with one spoke per lab, one per student, one per campaign, or a mixture is not something anyone can usefully decide in advance, and nothing here should force the decision. Anything whose records validate is a spoke.

JSON rather than YAML so it can be read and validated with no dependency beyond the validator itself -- these files are read on login nodes and in minimal CI containers.

standard_version.description: The version of the standard this MANIFEST is written against. Records declare their own `schema_version`, and a spoke may hold documents at several versions and usually will, because a bump never obliges a lab to rewrite data. So this is a default for records that declare nothing -- never a correction to records that do.

name.description: Human-readable name for this spoke. Free text: it is a label, not an identifier, and nothing joins on it.

granularity.description: What this spoke is organised around, for a reader's benefit only. Nothing validates or joins on it -- the field exists so the answer is written down somewhere rather than inferred from a directory listing. Any value is legitimate, including a mixture that changed over time.

layout.description: Which directories hold which kind of document. Every entry is a list, so one kind can live in several places -- a spoke with `2026-09-prbs/manifests/` and `2026-11-prbs/manifests/` lists both, or lists their parent and lets the walk recurse. Absent keys fall back to the default directory-name convention.

exclude.description: Paths the validator should not walk: scratch directories, vendored trees, notebook checkpoints. A spoke is allowed to contain things that are not records -- forcing every JSON file in a repository to be a valid document would make people keep their working files somewhere else, which is worse.

strict.description: When true, a JSON file whose kind cannot be inferred is an ERROR rather than a skip. Off by default, because a spoke legitimately holds configuration and notes. Turn it on once a spoke's layout has settled and you want a stray file to be noticed.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs in order to work in this spoke: how it is organised and why, what changed when, local conventions that diverge from the defaults.

extensions.description: Free-form. The validator ignores this rather than rejecting it -- the same escape hatch and the same promotion rule as every other document kind.

spoke_id.description: Stable identifier for this spoke. `name` is explicitly a label that nothing joins on, so without this a spoke can never be registered and nothing can cross-check a record's inherited stewards against the manifest that declares them. Required now because zero manifests exist anywhere, which makes it free today and a major bump later.

kind.description: Which side of the hub/spoke split this repository is on. Added because this manifest used to be a data-spoke concept only, which left analysis spokes with nowhere to record ownership at all.

maturity.description: The default rung for records in this spoke that make no claim of their own. Capped at `working` -- see the definition for why inheritance must not be able to manufacture a review.
